accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding protected areas in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Andhra Pradesh has one tiger reserve and one elephant reserve.
2. The State has three National Parks and thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries.
3. Seshachalam is the only Biosphere Reserve listed for Andhra Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh has one tiger reserve, one elephant reserve, one biosphere reserve, three National Parks and thirteen Wildlife Sanctuaries.
accepted.tq: Use the complete protected-area count and check whether all three statements fit the same administrative profile.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: According to the Andhra Pradesh State Forest Report 2024–25, notified forests covered approximately what proportion of the State’s geographical area?
accepted.x: The 2024–25 figure was 37,221.11 square kilometres, constituting 22.84% of the State’s area.
accepted.tq: Separate the reported percentage from the later revised figure and select the exact edition-specific value.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve?
o: It was notified in 2010 and extends across the Tirupati and Kurnool Forest Circles.
It was notified in 1996 and is Andhra Pradesh’s only tiger reserve.
It was notified in 2005 and lies exclusively in the Nallamala hills.
It was notified in 2020 and is located only in the Godavari estuary.
accepted.x: Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve was notified in 2010 and spans the Tirupati and Kurnool Circles.
accepted.tq: Match the protected area with its notification year and administrative location.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: The approximate area of the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is:
accepted.x: The reported area of Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve is 4,755.997 square kilometres.
accepted.tq: Read the numerical options carefully and identify the exact area associated with the named reserve.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s:
Which of the following species is associated with the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve?
1. Red Sanders
2. Cycas beddomei
3. Golden Gecko
4. Jerdon’s Courser
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Red Sanders, Cycas beddomei and the Golden Gecko are associated with Seshachalam. Jerdon’s Courser is associated with Sri Lankamalleswara Wildlife Sanctuary.
accepted.tq: Eliminate the species linked to a different protected area rather than treating all Andhra species as belonging to one reserve.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the Seshachalam Biosphere Reserve:
1. It contains 1,756 flowering plant species.
2. More than 220 bird species have been recorded there.
3. It includes the Sri Venkateswara National Park and Wildlife Sanctuary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The reserve has 1,756 flowering plant species, more than 220 bird species and includes Sri Venkateswara protected areas.
accepted.tq: Combine quantitative biodiversity data with the reserve’s constituent protected areas.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is situated in the:
accepted.x: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve is located in the Nallamala hills and is the largest tiger reserve in India by area.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the geographical setting of the tiger reserve from those of Papikonda and Coringa.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve had approximately how many tigers according to the All India Tiger Estimation 2022 figure cited?
accepted.x: The cited estimate for Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was 63–67 tigers.
accepted.tq: Use the range directly and avoid confusing the reserve’s tiger count with its area or State-level count.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Papikonda National Park primarily protects the:
o: mangrove forests of the Krishna delta
accepted.x: Papikonda National Park protects the Papikondalu ranges situated along the Godavari River.
accepted.tq: Associate the protected area with its defining landscape and river.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is best described as a protected area of:
o: alpine meadows in the Tirupati hills
mangroves in the Godavari estuary near Kakinada
dry deciduous forests in the Nallamala hills
accepted.x: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary is located near Kakinada and protects mangroves of the Godavari estuary. The Godavari–Krishna estuaries together form India’s second-largest mangrove ecosystem.
accepted.tq: Use the location–ecosystem combination to distinguish Coringa from inland sanctuaries.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Rollapadu is associated with the Great Indian Bustard, not the Golden Gecko. The Golden Gecko is associated with Seshachalam.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped species–sanctuary pair among otherwise familiar Andhra Pradesh associations.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the smallest National Park in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Rajiv Gandhi National Park at Rameswaram, Kadapa
accepted.x: Rajiv Gandhi National Park at Rameswaram in Kadapa is identified as Andhra Pradesh’s smallest National Park. It was established in 2005.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the smallest protected area from better-known parks by combining name, location and year.
accepted.sec: AP protected areas - Seshachalam, Papikonda, Coringa, NSTR

accepted.s: The National Gene Bank operated by the National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources primarily conserves:
accepted.x: NBPGR runs the National Gene Bank for plant and crop genetic resources. Livestock, fish and microorganisms are associated with NBAGR, NBFGR and NBAIM respectively.
accepted.tq: Identify the institution by its genetic-resource category and reject neighbouring ICAR bureaus.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below.

List-I (Institution)
a. NBAGR
b. NBFGR
c. NBAIM
d. NBPGR

List-II (Resource)
i. Plants and crops
ii. Animals and livestock
iii. Fish
iv. Agriculturally important microorganisms
accepted.x: NBAGR deals with livestock, NBFGR with fish, NBAIM with agriculturally important microorganisms and NBPGR with plants and crops.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive resource categories and complete the one-to-one institutional mapping.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: A stored sample of germplasm in a gene bank is technically referred to as an:
accepted.x: Each stored germplasm sample in a gene bank is called an accession.
accepted.tq: Test the exact technical term rather than the broader concept of germplasm conservation.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the National Gene Bank established through NBPGR?
o: It was set up in 1996 and holds about 4.7 lakh accessions through 12 regional stations.
It was set up in 2015 and stores only microbial cultures at four stations.
It was set up in 2005 and holds about 10 lakh livestock accessions through 12 zoos.
It was set up in 2025 and stores only crop wild relatives at one station.
accepted.x: The National Gene Bank was established in 1996, has about 4.7 lakh accessions and is supported by 12 regional stations.
accepted.tq: Combine the establishment year, accession count and network size instead of relying on a single number.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: The National Wildlife Genetic Resource Bank at Hyderabad is located at the:
o: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research
accepted.x: India’s first bank for DNA, tissues and embryos of endangered wild animals is located at Nehru Zoological Park, Hyderabad.
accepted.tq: Use the specific institutional location to distinguish a wildlife genetic resource bank from plant gene banks.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: Field gene banks are most suitable for conserving:
o: vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds
only orthodox seeds kept in dry cold storage
accepted.x: Field gene banks maintain living collections, especially of vegetatively propagated crops and crops with recalcitrant seeds, such as mango, coconut and banana.
accepted.tq: Apply the conservation method to the biological material that cannot be conveniently stored as orthodox seed.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly represents the figures relating to India’s crop wealth?
o: 902 cultivated species and 902 crop wild relatives
811 cultivated species and 811 crop wild relatives
902 cultivated species and 811 crop wild relatives
811 cultivated species and 902 crop wild relatives
accepted.x: India’s crop wealth is reported as 811 cultivated species and 902 crop wild relatives.
accepted.tq: Keep the two close numerical categories in their correct order.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly associates an international instrument with its principal concern in the context of crop genetic resources?
accepted.x: The International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture is linked with farmers’ rights. The Nagoya Protocol concerns access and benefit sharing, not the subjects listed in the other options.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between nearby international environmental instruments by their subject matter.
accepted.sec: Gene banks - institution and location; field gene banks; global crop gene banks

accepted.s: Cryopreservation generally uses which medium and temperature?
accepted.x: Cryopreservation is generally carried out in liquid nitrogen at −196°C, which halts metabolic activity and preserves viability for very long periods.
accepted.tq: Match the preservation method with its characteristic cryogenic medium and temperature.
accepted.sec: Cryopreservation - medium, temperature, materials

accepted.s:
Which of the following may be preserved through cryopreservation?
1. Gametes and embryos
2. Seeds and pollen
3. Disease-free meristems and tissues
4. DNA
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Cryopreservation can be applied to gametes, embryos, seeds, pollen, disease-free meristems, tissues and DNA. Therefore all four statements are correct.
accepted.tq: Treat the list as a materials question and check whether each biological material is included in the preservation range.
accepted.sec: Cryopreservation - medium, temperature, materials

accepted.s: The immediate biological effect of storing material in liquid nitrogen during cryopreservation is that it:
o: converts all tissues into permanent fossil material
destroys DNA but preserves only cell walls
increases metabolic activity and accelerates growth
halts metabolic activity while retaining viability
accepted.x: Liquid nitrogen at cryogenic temperature halts metabolic activity while allowing the preserved material to remain viable for decades or centuries.
accepted.tq: Infer the purpose of the technology from the relation between temperature, metabolism and viability.
accepted.sec: Cryopreservation - medium, temperature, materials

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden — Shibpur, Howrah
National Botanical Garden of CSIR-NBRI — Darjeeling
accepted.x: The Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden, known for the Great Banyan and associated with the Botanical Survey of India, is at Shibpur in Howrah, West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Use the location of the best-known garden as the sure pair and eliminate shifted locations.
accepted.sec: Botanical gardens - location

accepted.s: The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, described as the largest botanical garden in the list, is located in:
accepted.x: The Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, is located in London, United Kingdom.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the international garden from the Indian botanical gardens by location.
accepted.sec: Botanical gardens - location
